area: Claude Code native memory system — CLAUDE.md, auto memory, rule files, path scoping, imports, /doctor, /init, managed CLAUDE.md (as of 2026-09-20, per code.claude.com/docs/en/memory)

facts.behavior: "Claude Code has two complementary memory systems. Both are loaded at the start of every conversation. Claude treats them as context, not enforced configuration. To block an action regardless of what Claude decides, use a PreToolUse hook instead. The more specific and concise your instructions, the more consistently Claude follows them." CLAUDE.md: written by you, contains instructions/rules. Auto memory: written by Claude, contains learnings/patterns.
facts.limits: Neither system is a hard enforcement layer; only hooks (e.g. PreToolUse) block actions regardless of what the model decides.

facts.behavior: Four scopes, loaded broadest to most specific: Managed policy (macOS /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md, Linux/WSL /etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md, Windows C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md) — org-wide, all users; User (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md) — just you, all projects; Project (./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md) — team via source control; Local (./CLAUDE.local.md) — just you, current project, meant for .gitignore.
facts.limits: "CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md files in the directory hierarchy above the working directory are loaded at launch. Files in subdirectories load on demand when Claude reads files in those directories."

facts.behavior: "Run /init to generate a starting CLAUDE.md automatically. Claude analyzes your codebase and creates a file with build commands, test instructions, and project conventions it discovers. If a CLAUDE.md already exists, /init suggests improvements rather than overwriting it." It also migrates instructions from Cursor rules (.cursor/rules/, .cursorrules) and Copilot rules (.github/copilot-instructions.md) into the generated file.
facts.limits: With CLAUDE_CODE_NEW_INIT=1 set, /init instead runs an interactive multi-phase flow: asks which artifacts to set up (CLAUDE.md files, skills, hooks), explores the codebase with a subagent, fills gaps via follow-up questions, and presents a reviewable proposal before writing any files; this mode also migrates AGENTS.md, .devin/rules/, .windsurf/rules/ or .windsurfrules, and .clinerules.

facts.behavior: "Size: target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file. Longer files consume more context and reduce adherence. If your instructions are growing large, use path-scoped rules so instructions load only when Claude works with matching files."
facts.limits: This is a stated best-practice target, not an enforced cap (contrast with the hard 4 MiB skip limit, a separate fact).

facts.behavior: "Claude Code loads a CLAUDE.md file of up to 4 MiB in full and skips a larger file. Shorter files produce better adherence."
facts.limits: Applies to CLAUDE.md files specifically (contrast with MEMORY.md's 200-line/25KB startup-read limit).

facts.behavior: "CLAUDE.md files can import additional files using @path/to/import syntax. Imported files are expanded and loaded into context at launch alongside the CLAUDE.md that references them." Both relative (resolved relative to the file containing the import, not the working directory) and absolute paths are allowed. "Imported files can recursively import other files, with a maximum depth of four hops." Import parsing skips Markdown code spans and fenced code blocks; wrapping a path in backticks (`` `@README` ``) keeps it literal instead of importing it.
facts.limits: Max recursion depth of 4 hops. Splitting into imports helps organization but does not reduce context, since imported files still load at launch.

facts.behavior: "An import in a project-level memory file is external when its path resolves outside your working directory... The first time Claude Code encounters external imports in a project, it shows an approval dialog listing the files. If you decline, the imports stay disabled and the dialog doesn't appear again." User-scope memory files (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.claude/rules/) load their imports without the dialog and are trusted like the rest of personal config.
facts.limits: Exception: in Cowork sessions on desktop, Claude Code skips (does not load) any import in a user-scope file resolving outside the session's working directory, and skips a ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md or ~/.claude/rules/ that is itself a symlink/hard link pointing outside the working directory.

facts.behavior: "If you work across multiple git worktrees of the same repository, a gitignored CLAUDE.local.md only exists in the worktree where you created it. To share personal instructions across worktrees, import a file from your home directory instead" (e.g. @~/.claude/my-project-instructions.md).
facts.limits: CLAUDE.local.md itself is not shared across worktrees; only an import from outside the worktree achieves that.

facts.behavior: "Claude Code loads CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md from your current working directory and every directory above it." All discovered files are concatenated (not overriding each other); ordered root-down to the working directory, so instructions closer to the launch directory are read last; within a directory, CLAUDE.local.md is appended after CLAUDE.md. Subdirectory CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.local.md files are "included when Claude reads files in those subdirectories" rather than loaded at launch.
facts.limits: Subdirectory memory files load lazily (on file read), not at session start.

facts.feature: Block-level HTML comments stripped from CLAUDE.md
facts.behavior: "Block-level HTML comments (<!-- maintainer notes -->) in CLAUDE.md files are stripped before the content is injected into Claude's context. Use them to leave notes for human maintainers without spending context tokens on them. Comments inside code blocks are preserved. When you open a CLAUDE.md file directly with the Read tool, comments remain visible."
facts.limits: Only block-level comments outside code blocks are stripped from context; the file on disk is unchanged.

facts.behavior: "The --add-dir flag gives Claude access to additional directories outside your main working directory. By default, CLAUDE.md files from these directories are not loaded." Setting CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1 loads CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/*.md, and CLAUDE.local.md from the additional directory.
facts.limits: CLAUDE.local.md from the additional directory is skipped if 'local' is excluded from --setting-sources. This env var does not make AGENTS.md load from the additional directory.

facts.behavior: "For larger projects, you can organize instructions into multiple files using the .claude/rules/ directory... All .md files are discovered recursively, so you can organize rules into subdirectories." "Rules without paths frontmatter are loaded at launch with the same priority as .claude/CLAUDE.md."
facts.limits: "Project rules are skipped if you exclude project from --setting-sources. Before v2.1.211, rules that load on demand, including path-scoped rules and rules in nested .claude/rules/ directories, loaded even when project was excluded."

facts.behavior: "Rules can be scoped to specific files using YAML frontmatter with the paths field. These conditional rules only apply when Claude is working with files matching the specified patterns." "Rules without a paths field are loaded unconditionally and apply to all files. Path-scoped rules trigger when Claude reads files matching the pattern, not on every tool use." As of v2.1.198, matching also works through a symlinked path to the project directory. Glob patterns support brace expansion (e.g. src/**/*.{ts,tsx}).
facts.limits: A rule's whole paths list shares one budget of 1,000 expanded patterns and 4 MiB; patterns without braces don't count against it. Patterns exceeding the budget are used unexpanded (literal braces match nothing); before v2.1.217 this stalled/crashed the CLI at startup. An invalid glob (unmatched bracket) matches nothing but doesn't break the rule's other patterns; before v2.1.207 one invalid pattern made the Read tool fail for every file the rule was evaluated against.

facts.feature: Sharing rules across projects via symlinks
facts.behavior: "The .claude/rules/ directory supports symlinks, so you can maintain a shared set of rules and link them into multiple projects. Circular symlinks are detected and handled gracefully." "Claude Code treats a symlink whose target is outside your working directory like an external import. The linked rules don't load until you approve external imports for the project, and after that only the ones without a paths field load."
facts.limits: "Claude Code asks for that approval only when a project memory file imports a file outside the working directory with @path, not for symlinks alone." To avoid the approval requirement, keep shared rules in ~/.claude/rules/ instead.

facts.behavior: "Personal rules in ~/.claude/rules/ apply to every project on your machine." "User-level rules are loaded before project rules, giving project rules higher priority."
facts.limits: Scope: all projects on the machine, not just the current repo.

facts.behavior: Deployed at a fixed OS path (e.g. /etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md) via MDM/Group Policy/Ansible, or inline via the claudeMd key in managed-settings.json. "This file cannot be excluded by individual settings." Scope: "every Claude Code session on the machine, in every repository." Precedence: "Loads before user and project CLAUDE.md." Where honored: "managed and policy settings only. Setting claudeMd in user, project, or local settings has no effect."
facts.limits: "Settings rules are enforced by the client regardless of what Claude decides to do. CLAUDE.md instructions shape Claude's behavior but are not a hard enforcement layer." So while its inclusion is guaranteed and cannot be excluded, its prose content is still advisory to the model, not a hard block — the docs direct you to managed settings keys like permissions.deny or sandbox.enabled for actual technical enforcement.

facts.behavior: "The claudeMdExcludes setting lets you skip specific files by path or glob pattern... Patterns are matched against absolute file paths using glob syntax. You can configure claudeMdExcludes at any settings layer: user, project, local, or managed policy. Arrays merge across layers." A pattern matching either a symlinked rule file's own path or its link target excludes it (fixed in v2.1.239; before that only the link-target path worked).
facts.limits: "Managed policy CLAUDE.md files cannot be excluded. This ensures organization-wide instructions always apply regardless of individual settings."

facts.behavior: "Claude Code can read AGENTS.md as your project instructions, so a repository already set up for other coding agents works without adding a CLAUDE.md, an import, or a setting." By default Claude reads AGENTS.md only when there is no CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md, or CLAUDE.local.md in the working directory or above it; those three file types 'count' toward suppressing AGENTS.md, while ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the org's managed CLAUDE.md, and .claude/rules/ files do not.
facts.limits: Requires Claude Code v2.1.277+. Unavailable (falls back to CLAUDE.md-only, and the Project instructions setting is hidden in /config) on versions before that, in sessions that don't fetch feature flags from Anthropic (e.g. Amazon Bedrock, other third-party providers, or telemetry disabled), in the first session after install/upgrade to a version with support, or when disableAllHooks/allowManagedHooksOnly is set or the built-in agents-md plugin is disabled.

facts.feature: Project instructions setting (/config) controlling CLAUDE.md vs AGENTS.md loading
facts.behavior: Four values: claude-md-or-agents-md (default) — CLAUDE.md, or AGENTS.md only when no CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.local.md present; claude-md-and-agents-md — both, each directory's CLAUDE.md first then its AGENTS.md (already-loaded AGENTS.md not re-read if imported/symlinked); claude-md — CLAUDE.md files only; managed-only — "Only your organization's managed CLAUDE.md and auto memory at launch. Your project, local, and user CLAUDE.md files, your .claude/rules/ files, and every AGENTS.md are left out. A subdirectory's CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules/ files, and path-scoped rules, still load when Claude reads a file there."
facts.limits: Configurable via /config, or via pluginConfigs "agents-md@builtin" → options.instructionFiles in ~/.claude/settings.json, a --settings file, or managed settings; "Claude Code ignores it in project and local settings files." Takes effect from the next message sent and in new sessions.

facts.behavior: An AGENTS.md read through the Project instructions setting: does not appear in /memory or the /context Memory files list (verify via an 'AGENTS.md loaded' session line instead); InstructionsLoaded hooks don't fire for it (they do fire for an AGENTS.md a CLAUDE.md imports/symlinks to); its directory's AGENTS.md does not load via --add-dir + CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD (only CLAUDE.md does); an @path import of a file outside the working directory inside it loads with no approval prompt if external imports were already approved for the project (vs. CLAUDE.md, which prompts).
facts.limits: Not read: AGENTS.local.md, AGENTS.override.md, or anything under a .agents/ directory.

facts.feature: Sharing one instructions file via symlink or import (CLAUDE.md ↔ AGENTS.md)
facts.behavior: Put @AGENTS.md as an import at the top of CLAUDE.md, or symlink CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md (ln -s AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md). "Claude reads CLAUDE.md through the link, but the Edit and Write tools refuse to write through a symlink, and the refusal directs Claude to edit the link's target, AGENTS.md, instead."
facts.limits: On Windows, symlink creation needs Administrator privileges/Developer Mode, and Git checks out a committed symlink as plain text unless core.symlinks is enabled, so the import form is recommended instead of the symlink form for cross-platform repos.

facts.behavior: "You can also run /import to bring a supported coding agent's configuration into Claude Code, which appends a one-time copy of instruction files such as AGENTS.md to the matching CLAUDE.md and carries over MCP servers, commands, subagents, and skills. Requires Claude Code v2.1.213 or later."
facts.limits: One-time copy, not an ongoing sync.

facts.behavior: Claude saves four kinds of notes, recorded as a type field in the memory file's frontmatter: user (role, expertise, working preferences), feedback (corrections given, approaches confirmed), project (ongoing work, deadlines, decisions Claude can't derive from code/git history), reference (where to find information outside the project). "Claude skips anything it can derive from the codebase, such as architecture, file paths, or debugging fixes. It also skips anything your CLAUDE.md files already say." "Claude doesn't save something every session. It decides what's worth remembering based on whether the information would be useful in a future conversation."
facts.limits: Content selection is model-driven, not user-configured; the only user controls are enabling/disabling the system and editing files after the fact.

facts.behavior: "Auto memory is on by default. To toggle it, open /memory in a session and use the auto memory toggle, which saves autoMemoryEnabled to your user settings at ~/.claude/settings.json. To turn it off for a single project, set autoMemoryEnabled in that project's settings" (JSON: {"autoMemoryEnabled": false}). "To disable auto memory via environment variable, set CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1."
facts.limits: Three control points: /memory toggle (user settings), per-project settings.json, or env var.

facts.feature: Auto memory storage location and scope
facts.behavior: "Each project gets its own memory directory at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/. The <project> path is derived from the git repository, so all worktrees and subdirectories within the same repo share one auto memory directory. Outside a git repo, the project root is used instead." "Auto memory is machine-local... Files are not shared across machines or cloud environments." Can be redirected via autoMemoryDirectory in settings.json (any settings scope: user/project/local/policy/--settings; value must be absolute or start with ~/), or the project-dir name can be pinned via CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME (v2.1.234+) so multiple repos share one memory directory.
facts.limits: When permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories is on, "Claude Code loads no auto memory from a directory that a repository-supplied settings file chooses and saves none to it, wherever that directory sits"; a repo-supplied autoMemoryDirectory in .claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.local.json is honored only under the same workspace-trust rule as hooks in settings files.

facts.feature: Auto memory directory structure (MEMORY.md index + topic files)
facts.behavior: The directory contains MEMORY.md (index, one line per memory, loaded into every session) plus one topic file per memory (e.g. user_role.md, feedback_testing.md). "MEMORY.md acts as an index of the memory directory. Claude reads and writes files in this directory throughout your session, using MEMORY.md to keep track of what's stored where."
facts.limits: Topic files are not loaded at session start (see startup read-limit fact); only MEMORY.md is.

facts.behavior: "The first 200 lines of MEMORY.md, or the first 25KB, whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation. Content beyond that threshold is not loaded at session start." "After Claude writes to MEMORY.md, Claude Code measures the file against the 200-line and 25KB read limits. If the file is near a limit, Claude Code reminds Claude to shorten it: keep one line per entry, move detail into topic files, and merge or drop stale entries. If the file is over a limit, the write still succeeds, but Claude Code returns an error telling Claude to rewrite the index, because everything past the limit is dropped on the next load."
facts.limits: "This limit applies only to MEMORY.md," not to CLAUDE.md (which has the separate 4 MiB hard skip) or to topic files (not loaded at startup at all, read on demand via normal file tools).

facts.behavior: "The main conversation's auto memory isn't loaded into subagents; the exception is a fork, which inherits the parent conversation and system prompt. A subagent's own auto memory, enabled with the subagent memory field, is a separate directory."
facts.limits: Ordinary (non-fork) subagents start with no access to the parent conversation's auto memory.

facts.feature: Auto memory exempt from transcript cleanup
facts.behavior: "Claude Code deletes old session transcripts after the cleanupPeriodDays retention period, but excludes the memory files in the memory directory from that retention sweep. MEMORY.md and topic files stay until you or Claude edits or deletes them."
facts.limits: Only manual/Claude-driven edits or deletes remove memory files; time-based cleanup does not.

facts.behavior: "When Claude writes a memory file that begins with YAML frontmatter, Claude Code records the write time in a modified frontmatter field as an ISO 8601 timestamp. The timestamp shows how current the fact is, both to you and to Claude when it reads the memory back. Any file that has frontmatter gets the field the next time Claude writes it, including files created on earlier versions; Claude Code never adds frontmatter to a file that has none."
facts.limits: Requires Claude Code v2.1.214+; only applied to files that already have frontmatter.

facts.behavior: "The /memory command lists your CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, and other memory file locations across user and project scopes, including user and project CLAUDE.md entries for files that don't exist yet. It also lets you toggle auto memory on or off and provides an option to open the auto memory folder. Select any file to open it in your editor; selecting one that doesn't exist yet creates it first."
facts.limits: GUI editors (e.g. VS Code) open in a separate window and the session stays usable while it's open (before v2.1.216, /memory waited for the file to close). Terminal editors (e.g. Vim) take over the terminal until you exit.

facts.behavior: "To check which CLAUDE.md and rules files loaded into the current session, run /context." Also used to confirm a given CLAUDE.md loaded, via the list under Memory files.
facts.limits: "AGENTS.md appears there only when a CLAUDE.md imports it, not when Claude reads it directly."

facts.behavior: "The /doctor checkup proposes trims for a checked-in CLAUDE.md: it cuts content Claude can derive from the codebase, such as directory layouts, dependency lists, and architecture overviews, and keeps pitfalls, rationale, and conventions that differ from tool defaults."
facts.limits: "The trim check requires Claude Code v2.1.206 or later." It proposes trims (a suggestion), described alongside other memory troubleshooting rather than as an automatic rewrite.

facts.feature: CLAUDE.md delivered as user message, not system prompt
facts.behavior: "CLAUDE.md content is delivered as a user message after the system prompt, not as part of the system prompt itself. Claude reads it and tries to follow it, but there's no guarantee of strict compliance, especially for vague or conflicting instructions."
facts.limits: For instructions needing system-prompt-level weight, docs point to --append-system-prompt instead; for instructions needing guaranteed execution at a lifecycle point, docs point to hooks instead.

facts.behavior: "For instructions you want at the system prompt level, use --append-system-prompt. You pass it at launch, so it's better suited to scripts and automation than interactive use."
facts.limits: Launch-time only flag, not an interactive/session command. Content is still advisory to the model even once placed in the system prompt.

facts.behavior: "Use the InstructionsLoaded hook to log which CLAUDE.md and rules files are loaded, when they load, and why. This is useful for debugging path-specific rules or lazy-loaded files in subdirectories."
facts.limits: Does not fire for an AGENTS.md read directly via the Project instructions setting (only for CLAUDE.md/imported or symlinked AGENTS.md). It logs load events; it does not itself block anything.

facts.behavior: "Project-root CLAUDE.md survives compaction: after /compact, Claude re-reads it from disk and re-injects it into the session. Nested CLAUDE.md files in subdirectories and rules with paths: frontmatter reload as Claude reads files they apply to."
facts.limits: "If an instruction disappeared after compaction, it was given only in conversation, lives in a nested CLAUDE.md that hasn't reloaded yet, or is a path-scoped rule that hasn't matched a file since."

facts.behavior: "@ file references add CLAUDE.md in the file's directory and parent directories to context." "Directory references show file listings, not contents." Type @ to open a path suggestion menu; can reference MCP resources with @server:resource syntax too.
facts.limits: Directory references only list files; they don't pull file contents into context the way a file reference does.
